overall_reason: The visitor mode is Persuade (an AI video studio landing page); the provider list is honest and footnoted ('All trademarks belong to their respective owners'), and the sweep's five INT-002 'Vertex' hits are on 'Google Cloud Vertex AI', a real Google product the footer names as a provider, so I judge them the brand's own true statement; what pads the page is two unbacked labels of standing: 'The world's first full-cycle studio' and 'The world's top 5 LLMs' (which names three).

score.reason: T-PROOF-SOURCE fails on 'The world's first full-cycle studio' (INT-022, Reflex) and T-FIGURE-AUDIT on 'The world's top 5 LLMs' with no ranking (INT-011, Reflex); T-PROOF-SWAP passes because the page shows no testimonials or customer logos.

findings.evidence: The closing block says 'The world's first full-cycle studio. From idea and brainstorm to final render with Google Veo and Advanced ID System.' Nothing on the page backs 'world's first': no date, no comparison and no source. The same claim style appears on the first screen as an orange 'TOP' pill beside 'FEATURED MODEL' on the carousel (tiles/1440-00.png). Draft INT-115 asks for ranking data behind leadership claims.
findings.after: Cut 'world's first' and say what the studio does: 'A full-cycle studio: brainstorm, script, characters and final render in one project.'
findings.why: A 'first' claim is checkable by any visitor who knows the field, and several all-in-one AI video studios exist; the unbacked superlative costs the real feature list its credibility.

findings.where: 'Ecosystem of studios', Brainstorm Room card, 1440; tiles/1440-04.png
findings.evidence: The card says 'The world's top 5 LLMs — Claude Sonnet, DeepSeek, Gemini — in one room for writing your scripts.' The claims table lists it under awards_badges and social_proof. The line names three models for a 'top 5', and it cites no ranking, benchmark or date. Draft INT-115 asks for an as-of date and ranking data.
findings.before: "The world's top 5 LLMs — Claude Sonnet, DeepSeek, Gemini"
findings.after: Name all the models the room offers, without a ranking: 'Claude Sonnet, DeepSeek, Gemini and two more models in one room.'
findings.why: The ranking is a claim about other companies' products; it carries no source and lists fewer models than it counts.

strengths: The footer names every provider and disclaims ownership: 'Cineyx AI uses the power of Google Vertex AI, Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, Vidu, Wan, Seedance, ElevenLabs, and other providers ... All trademarks belong to their respective owners.'
The signup offer is stated in full on the first screen ('Sign up today: 50 AI Energy + 1 Free Character') with no countdown or stock count.
The page shows no testimonials, ratings, user counts or customer logos.
not_investigated: authenticity against outside sources: the lens does not browse, so any claim only the web could settle is not verified
checkout, signup and cancellation flows beyond the captured page
countdown or counter behaviour on reload: the capture does not reload to compare
the before and after examples under 'What you can actually create' ('Here's what people make with Cineyx') could not be checked as real outputs of the product
the model names ('MiniMax H3', 'Seedance 2.5', 'Gemini 3 Pro', 'CineCore Fast') could not be checked

the 'Send feedback' action showed a progress state after its request finished; that is the sweep's CMP-001 stuck_spinner hit, not an integrity call
